name: Pre-treated lithium brine; at plant
description: This unit process produces pre-treated brine from brine sources in Canada by removing hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and ionic sulfides, to make it suitable for direct lithium extraction using adsorption. The functional unit is 1 kg pre-treated brine. The gate-to-gate system boundary includes gas striping and H2S polishing of incoming un-treated brine. Ozone generation is included in the system boundary.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Key consumption data comes from a industrial report published in 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The brine concentrations are based on average Canadian values however, the process may be used in other regions in which the brine concentrations are similar.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Removal of H2S is achieved by adding hydrochloric acid (HCl) to lower pH and subsequent gas stripping based on amine sweetening system. Also, remaining sulfides are removed from the gas using ozone as oxidizing agent. Ozone is generated on-site by an ozonation unit. Oxygen required for ozonation is generated by pressure swing absorption of atomospheric air. Please view the flow diagram below for additional information.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional and gate to gate process.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This unit process for the pre-treatment of brine is based off a 20,000 metric ton of lithium hydroxide monohydrate production plant scale.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process is not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The electricity and chemical consumption data for brine pre-treatment are based on a prospective direct lithium extraction (DLE) project in Canada. These consumption values are proportional to dissolved H2S and ionic sulfides in Canadian brines.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Electricity and chemical consumption values were normalized based on amount of pre-treated brine production.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:
Boundary Conditions: The gate-to-gate system boundary includes gas striping and H2S polishing of incoming un-treated brine. Ozone generation is included in the system boundary.
Data Collection: Data was extracted from an industry report and brine composition measurement data.
Uncertainty: Uncertainty was not evaluated for this process.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process was developed to be an input to lithium hydroxide monohydrate production. The direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology is described under the unit process for Lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH.H2O).

reviews.details: Mass and energy balances were externally reviewed. LCA methodological aspects and comparison with literature were internally reviewed.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
SITUATION C1 -- ACCOUNTING The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook’s Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C1 do consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.

The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.
